name: relativistic precession -- inner vs outer orbit
description: Two test masses around a DIFFUSE central mass (large softening epsilon, so |Phi_g| stays in the 1PN-valid range everywhere -- no spurious near-core repulsion). The OUTER mass holds a stable, nearly-closed orbit (weak field -> little precession). The INNER, tighter orbit precesses strongly each pass -> a fast rosette. The contrast is the point: the closer in, the more relativistic and the larger the precession, heading toward the instability that defines the ISCO. Honest precession only, NOT an inspiral: both orbits are conservative (no energy loss), so neither spirals in -- a real inspiral needs radiated energy, which we do not fake. Toggle force tier to 'newtonian' and both close into fixed ellipses.
